newsitem.title: JAPAN: Idemitsu Petrochemical cuts ethylene output by 12%.
newsitem.headline: Idemitsu Petrochemical cuts ethylene output by 12%.

text.p: Idemitsu Petrochemical Co Ltd said on Tuesday it had cut ethylene production at its 365,000 tonne-per-year Chiba plant by 12 percent due to unfavourable conditions in the petrochemical product market.

The company has decided to cut ethylene output in an effort to help raise wholesale prices for its petrochemical products, which have failed to keep up with bullish naphtha prices, an Idemitsu Petrochemical spokesman said.
Naphtha is used as feedstock in ethylene production.

Near-term naphtha prices on Asia"s benchmark open-specification forward contract grew by about 33 percent in the second half of 1996 due to high global crude prices, and have remained firm so far this year amid tight supplies.

Idemitsu Petrochemical has not changed ethylene output levels at its Tokuyama plant, which has an annual output capacity of 450,000 tonnes, but it does not rule out the possibility of future production cuts at the plant, he said.

The spokesman said the petrochemical firm would continue to cut output at its Chiba plant "for the time being" while carefully watching for any changes in wholesale prices for its ethylene-derived petrochemical products.
